query: What quasi-experimental instruments (compulsory schooling reforms, childcare expansions, migration shocks, benefit RD cutoffs) most credibly identify maternal education and time-use effects regionally?

response.query: What quasi-experimental instruments (compulsory schooling reforms, childcare expansions, migration shocks, benefit RD cutoffs) most credibly identify maternal education and time-use effects regionally?
response.answer: Compulsory schooling reforms and benefit RD cutoffs most credibly identify maternal education and time-use effects regionally. Childcare expansions and migration shocks also provide valuable quasi-experimental insights.

results.title: Soldier of Fortune: The Shadowy Legacy of SAS Veteran Simon Mann
results.content: From Eton to Equatorial Guinea, Simon Mann’s life was a high-stakes gambit of privilege, power, and private warfare that ended not with a coup, but with a cautionary tale. From Eton to Equatorial Guinea, Simon Mann’s life was a high-stakes gambit of privilege, power, and private warfare that ended not with a coup, but with a cautionary tale. A former SAS officer and co-founder of Executive Outcomes and Sandline International, Mann’s name became synonymous with the 2004 “Wonga Coup,” a failed attempt to overthrow the oil-rich government of Equatorial Guinea. Mann ultimately served about five years behind bars in Africa, split between prisons in Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea. News of his death made headlines due to his notoriety as the man behind the “Wonga Coup.” From aristocratic officer to mercenary to international prisoner, Mann played a central role in shaping the modern private military industry.
